title: Anchored Model Release: Input/Output Schema and Behavioral Stability Charter
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define a formal, machine-checkable charter for "anchored" (customer-pinned) model releases that specifies allowed input formats, stable output shapes, tunable parameter ranges, and behavioral tolerances. The charter must be usable by model engineers, runtime, and the Console to enforce compatibility, generate onboarding checklists, and drive automated regression tests and publishing of performance profiles.
acceptance_criteria: A human-readable charter document exists describing: input schema (prompt fields, metadata, special tokens), output schema (message envelopes, structured JSON fields), mandatory/optional parameters, and backward-compatibility guarantees for the next 12 months.
A JSON Schema (v7) artifact that runtime can use to validate request payloads for anchored releases is checked into models/charters/ in the repo and linked from the model catalog.

A compatibility matrix mapping: parameter->allowed range/enum, parameter-change-safety (safe|may-affect-output|breaking), and required runtime behavior (ignore unknown params|reject) is published alongside the pinned release.
Automated onboarding pipeline validates 5 canonical prompt families and 10 edge-case prompts against the charter and produces a regression report and perf profile (latency and cost) for the release.
Console UI shows a clear 'anchored contract' view for pinned models with links to charter, schemas, perf profile, and recommended client-side mitigations.
Upgrade flow: contributors can propose non-breaking changes via a documented proposal PR; breaking changes require explicit user opt-in and a migration guide.
Security review flag set if charter exposes sensitive metadata or requires new privileges (KMS/HSM changes).
implementation_notes: Work will be split across runtime (validation hooks + enforcement), model onboarding (charter authoring templates), Console (UI to display contract), and CI (automated regression harness).
Start with a minimal JSON Schema covering: top-level request envelope, prompt array/object shapes, model_args block (temperature, max_tokens, top_p, stop sequences), and streaming boundary behavior.
Define a stable canonical output envelope: {id, choices: [{text, delta, index, logprobs?}], usage} and a clear policy for optional fields (e.g., logprobs may be omitted without breaking contract).
Runtime should support an 'compatibility_mode' flag per pinned release: strict (reject unknown), tolerant (ignore unknown), and shim (map deprecated params to new ones).
Add hooks to record contract violations to observability with a dedicated metric (contract.violation.count) and sample payloads for SRE triage.
Model engineers must supply 5 representative prompts and 3 adversarial prompts with expected invariants (e.g., structured JSON field must be present, enum values stable).
Publish the performance profile as a small JSON alongside the charter with percentiles for 128/512/2048 token sequences and recommended batching knobs.
milestones: M1: Charter template + JSON Schema draft (due 2026-02-27)
M3: Onboarding CI + regression harness running against 2 internal models (due 2026-03-13)
M5: Internal doc + handbook for model teams (due 2026-03-21)
risks: Overly strict schema will break legitimate client variants — prefer opt-in strict enforcement for the first 3 months.
Runtime enforcement complexity for streaming outputs (partial deltas) may require incremental rollout to avoid user-facing regressions.
Incomplete representative prompts from model teams could give false confidence for regression detection.
Performance profile publishing may leak sensitive cost signals if not scrubbed; coordinate with pricing/compliance.
